sentences.text: Dr. T. Balachander S/O Late. Mallaiah vs The District Collector,
Ranga Reddy
... on 4 November, 2024

Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.22346 of 2006
Order:

Heard Sri B.Chandrasen Reddy, learned Senior Counsel, representing Sri P.Venkata Swamy, learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent No.1, Sri L.Prabhakar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent No.2,
and Sri K.V.Bhanu Prasad, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3 and perused the record.

2. The present Writ Petition is filed assailing the action of the respondents-authorities in laying road in petitioners' plots bearing Nos.16, 17 and 18 admeasuring 766 square yards in Sy.Nos.232 and 239 situated at Manikonda Jagir Village and Gram Panchayat, Rajendranagar Mandal, Ranga Reddy district, without acquiring and without initiating any proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (for short, 'the Act'), as being illegal and arbitrary.

3. Petitioners contend that though the authorities have issued preliminary notification under Section 4(1) of the Act on 18.11.2005, the names of the petitioners were not mentioned therein in respect of the land sought to be acquired, nor their names were shown in the draft declaration issued on 13.12.2005.

4. Petitioners further contend that even in the award dt.16.01.2006, the names of the petitioners have not been mentioned for the petitioners to have knowledge of their plots being acquired for the purpose of laying of road by the respondents-authorities.

5. Petitioners also contend that the subject plots of land have been purchased by them under three registered documents, bearing Nos.4239/05, 4214/05 and 4242/05, executed on 30.03.2005 and registered on 31.03.2005, and as such, the names of the petitioners ought to have been reflected in the preliminary notification which was issued by the respondents-authorities under Section 4(1) of the Act on 18.11.2005, pursuant to a requisition received from the requisitioning authorities dt.22.10.2005.
6.

Petitioners contend that since the names of the petitioners are not shown in the preliminary notification, the action of the respondents- authorities in laying a road from the petitioners land without initiating any proceedings under the Act would have to be declared as illegal act violating Articles 14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.
Dr. T. Balachander S/O Late. Mallaiah vs The District Collector, Ranga Reddy ...

Counter-affidavits on behalf of the respondents have been filed denying the averments made by the petitioners.

8. Learned Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the 1st respondent submits that the authorities on receiving requisition dt.22.10.2005, had issued preliminary notification under Section 4(1) of the Act on 18.11.2005; that the same was published in the Gazette under Section 6 of the Act on 13.12.2005; that thereafter, an award was passed on 16.01.2006; and that possession of the subject plots of land was handed over on 30.01.2006.

9. Learned Government Pleader further submits that on the respondents-authorities passing the award on 16.01.2006, the compensation amount as determined in the aforesaid award was deposited with the concerned Civil Court on 10.03.2006 and it is only thereafter, the petitioners had approached the respondents-authorities and submitted representation dt.22.04.2006, and as such,
the said representation of the petitioners cannot be considered by the respondents-authorities,
since, the compensation amount has already been deposited into the Civil Court.
10.

By stating as above, learned Government Pleader submits that since the amount is already deposited into the concerned Civil Court, it is open for the petitioners to approach the concerned Court to claim the amount of compensation by establishing their title to the subject property.
11. I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.

12. Section 4 of the Act (as applicable in the State of Andhra Pradesh) provides that wherever it appears to the appropriate Government or District Collector that land in any locality is needed or is likely to be needed for any public purpose, a notification to the that effect shall be published in the official gazette or District Gazette and in two daily newspapers circulating in that locality of which one shall be in the regional language.
13. The notification that is required to be published in terms of Section 4 of the Act shall invariably contain the details of the lands that are required for public purpose, or for a company.

Though the respondents- authorities have issued notification under Section 4 of the Act, for public purpose, i.e.,
for the purpose of laying of road, the said preliminary notification did not mention the names of the petitioners being the owners of Plot Nos.16, 17 and 18 purchased by them from the 3rd respondent herein, under registered sale deeds dt.31.03.2005.
14.

On the other hand, the preliminary notification issued by the respondents-authorities showed the name of the 3rd respondent as occupier, which had converted the said land into plots and sold the same to various intending purchasers, like the petitioners, even before issuance of the preliminary notification.

15. Thus, the action of the respondents-authorities in showing the name of the 3rd respondent as occupier in the preliminary notification only goes to show that the respondents-authorities without actually taking into consideration the persons who are in possession of the subject land, had mentioned the name of the 3rd respondent as occupier, despite it having divested of his interest Dr. T. 2 over the subject land, by executing a registered sale deeds in favour of intending purchasers, like the petitioners.
16. Further, the respondents-authorities on issuing preliminary notification under Section 4 of the Act are required to undertake survey of the land sought to be acquired.

If only such a survey was undertaken, at least then the authorities could have noticed that the subject land, which is sought to be acquired for the public purpose, i.e., for laying of road, does not belong to 3rd respondent, having sold the same in favour of the petitioners, thereby requiring to issue amendment to include the names of the petitioners as owners.
Further, the authority by issuing amendment to preliminary notification, including the names of petitioners, could have called for objections for the proposed acquisition.

The respondents for the reasons best known to them did not undertake the aforesaid exercise, and on the other hand, proceeded with the acquisition by showing the name of the 3rd respondent as occupier and passed an award, on 16.01.2006, and thereafter, deposited the amount into the Civil Court, for the petitioners to run around the Civil Court in order to claim compensation in respect of their plots through which the respondents-authorities have laid the subject road.

17. Though on behalf of the respondents, it is sought to be contended by the learned Government Pleader that since, an award is passed and the amount has been deposited into the Civil Court, the petitioners can approach the concerned Court to claim compensation, it is to be noted that an award passed in the name of a wrong person has to be held as null and void and the real owner cannot be made to run to Civil Court in order to claim compensation under a proceeding or award that has been passed by the authorities wrongly.
18.

If the aforesaid course of action suggested by the learned Government Pleader is accepted, then the authorities would pass awards in the name of unconnected persons, as against the real owners,
and deposit the amount into the Court and take possession of the land by dispossessing the actual owners from the subject land, making the real owners to run from pillar to post to establish their title and interest to the property to claim compensation for the said land.

19. In similar circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in K ulsum R. Nadiadw ala v/ s. State of M aharashtra and others 1 by referring to the judgment of the Apex Court in Collector v/ s. Raja Ram Jaisw al 2 had held that since the mandatory requirement as required under Section (2012) 6 SCC 348 (1985) 3 SCC 1 4(1) of the Act is not complied with by the respondents while acquiring the lands in question, the entire acquisition proceedings required to be declared as null and void.

sentences.text: 20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforesaid decision also referred to the decision in J & K Housing Board v/ s. K unw ar Sanjay K rishan K aul 3 , wherein the Apex Court had held that all the formalities of serving notice to the interested person, stipulated under Section 4 of the Act, has to be mandatorily complied with in the manner provided therein, even though the interested persons have knowledge of the acquisition proceedings.

entities.text: J & K Housing Board v/ s. K unw ar Sanjay K rishan K aul 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Apex Court further held as under:
'when any statutory provision provides a particular manner for doing a particular act,
the said thing or act must be done in accordance with the manner prescribed therefor in the Act.

Merely because the parties concerned were aware of the acquisition Dr. T. Balachander S/O Late. Mallaiah vs The District Collector, Ranga Reddy ... on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147714299/
3 proceedings or served with individual notices, does not make the position alter when the statute makes it very clear that all the procedures/modes have to be strictly complied with in the manner provided therein.

Merely, because the landowners failed to submit their objections within 15 days, after the publication of notification under Section 4(1) of the Act, the authorities cannot be permitted to claim that it need not be strictly resorted to.' (2011) 10 SCC 714 21.

Further, this Court in G.Subba Rao v/ s. Governm ent of Andhra Pradesh 4 had held that mere taking of possession, without passing an award and without paying compensation, is fatal, insofar as issuance of notification under Section 4(1) and passing of award under Section 11 of the Act is concerned, and the possession of the land taken would not make the action of the respondents-authorities valid and justified for the Court to approve such action.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
22. In the instant case, since, the preliminary notification under Section 4(1) and award under Section 11 of the Act was issued/passed by the respondents-authorities without mentioning the names of the petitioners, though proposed land to be acquired thereunder for the purpose of laying of road belonged to the petitioners, being a mandatory requirement as required under Section 4 of the Act to be complied with by the respondents and inasmuch as the said requirement is not complied with, the claim of the authorities of passing award on 16.01.2006, taking possession on 30.01.2006 and thereafter depositing the amount before the Civil Court on 10.03.2006, would not ipso facto make the award valid, insofar as the extent of land of the petitioners affected by the said road widening.
1992 (2) ALT 608 23.

As the respondents-authorities having laid a road through the petitioners' land without acquiring the same as prescribed under the Act, and also having dispossessed the petitioners therefrom, the claim of the respondents-authorities of an award having been passed and the compensation amount being deposited before the Civil Court, in the considered view of this Court by itself would not justify the action of the respondents-authorities for being upheld, and thus, the entire acquisition proceedings requires to be declared as null and void.

24. Since, the respondents-authorities have dispossessed the petitioners from the subject plots bearing Nos.16, 17 and 18, purchased by them way back in the year 2006, without following due process of law, this Court is of the view that the respondents-authorities are to be directed to initiate land acquisition proceedings now under the Act 30 of 2013 within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and make necessary payment of compensation to the extent of land from which the petitioners were dispossessed.
25. Subject to the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
26. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
